posts.author: aLostSolo
posts.body:
Hello,
I have a question that has been bothering me for a while with the way waterfalls were intended to be designed in RPG Maker MV:
When mapping a waterfall and adding events for the spray effects, which is what the animation in "!Other2.png" file seems to be intended for, the water always look like it's way off from the waterfall's top and bottom at the edges.
I even searched to see if someone did it different in a tutorial and found this:
If you check one of the comments, someone even doubted this is really the way it was intended to be used.
(BTW I personally used the bigger spray at the bottom and the smaller one at the top but it still looks the same...)
Now my question is - Is this the right way and it's supposed to look like this? Or am I missing something?
Thanks

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
aLostSolo said:
Now my question is - Is this the right way and it's supposed to look like this? Or am I missing something?
Click to expand...
i cant speak to a "right" or "wrong" way to go about it, but the engine has sample maps available if you rightclick the little map directory and choose "load". some have waterfalls with mist, and the video uses the same technique the sample maps do to add it, so that i suppose would count as being intended (the thicker mist is on the bottom though)
aLostSolo said:
the water always look like it's way off from the waterfall's top and bottom at the edges.
Click to expand...
you could always make edits to it with an image editing software to be more in line with what you expect out of it. increasing the cell size a little vertically would let you visually place the mist closer to the top and bottom edges of the waterfall. Also if you have yanfly plugins, you can manually place them where you want them with the doodad plugin

posts.body:
Whoa, I didn't notice they used that in the sample maps...!
I guess that does make it sort of "intended"...
Thanks for that and for the tip! I will check Yanfly's plugin too.
